# connection:snap-fit-roller-axle

**Two barbed cantilever fingers over a 36.5000 mm plate — the foot's snap onto the ankle (it is not a roller mount)**

## What it joins

- **a** — the foot's barbed finger pair (part:microduck-foot-left / -right, interface 'roller_slot'): two cantilevers running along x 45.0000..55.0000 (10.0000 mm) at y ~0.5 and ~36.5, topped at z -12.3419, with a 33.47 deg lead-in narrowing the gap 36.0890 -> 34.7000 mm over 1.0500 mm of rise, a 34.7000 mm barb land 0.6000 mm tall (z -14.0000..-13.4000), barbs 1.0000 mm proud per side, and a 36.7000 mm pocket below
- **b** — the ankle's wide plate (part:microduck-ankle-left / -right, interface 'foot_snap_plate'): y 0.1632..36.6632 = 36.5000 mm across at z -15.5000..-15.0000, stepping down to 33.7000 mm above z -14.5000. It sits in the 36.7000 mm pocket at 0.1000 mm per side with the barbs 0.9000 mm over its shoulder.

## Verdict: PASS

THE SNAP IS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES AND THE BODY IT CAPTURES IS IDENTIFIED BY MEASUREMENT. Fingers (foot_left.stl, cecad.meshfeatures.intervals): two cantilevers running along x, spanning exactly x 45.0000..55.0000 at both y 0.0 and y 37.0 and at z -12.5/-12.6/-13.0; top z -12.3419 (the foot's own bbox maximum). Their inner gap as a function of height is monotonic in three regimes: a LEAD-IN 36.0890 (z -12.3500) -> 35.4590 (-12.8000) -> 34.7000 (-13.4000), i.e. 0.6945 mm per side over 1.0500 mm of rise, a 33.47 deg half-angle; a BARB LAND of 34.7000 mm held from z -13.4000 to -14.0000 (0.6000 mm tall); and a POCKET of 36.7000 mm from z -14.5000 down. The barbs therefore stand 1.0000 mm proud per side, which is exactly what part:microduck-foot-left's own row recorded. Plate (ankle_left.stl, same instrument): at x 50 the ankle spans y 0.1632..36.6632 = 36.5000 mm at z -15.0000 and -15.5000, and narrows to 1.5630..35.2630 = 33.7000 mm at z -14.5000 and above. So the plate sits in the 36.7000 mm pocket at 0.1000 mm PER SIDE, clears the 34.7000 mm barb land by 0.5000 mm per side where it is narrow, and needs 0.9000 mm of deflection per finger to pass it where it is wide. ONE MEASURED CORRECTION is recorded rather than smoothed: the foot's row called this the clip-on ROLLER's slot, and no roller is placed here in anything Pollen ships -- roller_blade, tire and rim occur in exactly one of the four MJCF files, robot_allcollisions_rollers.xml, which contains no foot or sole geom at all and swaps the ankle for ankle_l_v1/ankle_r_v1 (whose vertical Ø2.2/Ø3.5 at x 50.1090, y -5.5000 matches roller_blade's own Ø1.6 pilot at the same point, where ankle_left's is at 50.0000, 4.5020). What stays CANNOT DETERMINE is the SNAP FORCE, and the reason is named: the deflection (0.9000 mm) and the finger section are measurable, the printed PLA's modulus and strain limit at this layer orientation are in no file here, and no cantilever formula is offered in their place.

Deflection and section are measured; the printed PLA's modulus and permissible strain at this layer orientation are not in any file here, and a cantilever formula fed a guessed modulus would be a number with no source.

holds_by form: two barbs 1.0000 mm proud standing over a 0.9000 mm shoulder. transmits axial AND shear: this is the joint that stops the foot lifting off, which connection:snap-fit-ankle-blocks explicitly does not do (its pockets are open in z).
